model.name: Alias / Same-as Mapping
model.purpose: A reusable mixin for federated identity equivalence: an attributable assertion that two or more identifiers denote the same subject, qualified by asserting authority, predicate strength and confidence, scope conditions, supporting and refuting evidence, and a governed lifecycle status with immutable transition history.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-036 models the alias/same-as assertion as a first-class, addressable record that can be mixed into any host model whose subjects carry identifiers issued by more than one authority. Its boundary covers assertion identity and versioning; the equivalence predicate and asserted strength (strict identity versus context-scoped interchangeability); participating identifier endpoints held as references only; asserting authority and confidence qualification; scope and applicability conditions; references to supporting and refuting evidence; and the full lifecycle of the assertion (candidate/proposed, under-review, active, disputed, superseded, retracted, rejected, expired, tombstoned) with allowed and forbidden transitions, entry and exit conditions, responsible-authority attribution, effective intervals separated from record time, and an append-only transition history preserving prior decisions, reasons, reviewers, evidence references, supersession links and tombstones. The model is format-neutral: JSON, YAML, Markdown, RDF, Git, MCP or MongoDB are projections of these semantics. It does not own the identifiers or endpoints themselves, does not compute matches, does not resolve or redirect, does not decide authorization and does not mutate master data.
in_scope: Assertion record identity, addressability and append-only version history
Equivalence predicate and asserted strength, from strict identity to context-scoped interchangeability
Asserting authority, confidence qualification and scope/applicability conditions of the assertion
Lifecycle status vocabulary and its normative per-status consumption rules
Allowed and forbidden state transitions with entry and exit conditions and terminality
Attribution of the responsible decision authority and delegation reference for each transition
Immutable transition records carrying prior status, new status, change kind, reason, reviewer and evidence references
Distinction between correction, supersession, retraction, endpoint-deprecation notice, replacement/redirect notice, authority withdrawal and evidence expiry
Effective (validity) intervals separated from decision, observation and ingestion time
Supersedes / superseded-by, disputes / disputed-by and replaced-by links between assertions
Tombstone content and post-retraction readability of the assertion record
Detection and representation of conflicting simultaneous statuses, invalid transition attempts, late-arriving events, retroactive corrections and rollback requests
out_of_scope: Lifecycle, registration, deprecation or minting of the identifiers and endpoints referenced by the assertion
Execution of resolution, redirection or content negotiation for any endpoint
Computation of similarity, match scores, blocking or clustering by an entity-resolution engine
Authorization decisions: whether a principal may read or write an assertion is evaluated by the referenced access-policy model
Creation, merge, split or any other mutation of master-data or host-entity records
Platform access audit trails, log retention and enforcement engines
Physical execution of disposition, erasure or storage-level deletion
Definition of the domain evidence itself (survey results, document scans, reconciliation reports) beyond references to it
Cryptographic notarisation, timestamping authorities and trust-service governance

boundary_notes.distinction: This model references endpoints and records the assertion-side consequence of an endpoint becoming deprecated or replaced. Endpoint status, permanence and any redirect execution remain owned by the endpoint registry, which follows its own non-reclamation and deprecation rules.

A match score may be referenced as evidence for an assertion, but scoring functions, thresholds and blocking strategies are owned by the resolution model. This model records only the assertion, its qualification and its status.

The transition record names the agent recorded as responsible and cites the governing decision policy; whether that agent was permitted to act is evaluated and enforced elsewhere. Citing a policy never grants this model evaluation or enforcement semantics.

The transition history is a domain record of status decisions about assertions; it is not the platform's access audit trail and does not replace it. Neither substitutes for the other, and this model defines no audit-trail semantics.

This model states what must survive retraction and what a tombstone must retain; the retention schedule, disposition authority and execution of disposal are owned by the adopting Dimension's records policy.

Transition records align with provenance activities and attributions but are not a general provenance store. PROV invalidation implies an entity is no longer available for use; a retracted assertion here remains readable as a tombstoned record, so the alignment is partial and declared, not conformant.

The mixin attaches assertion status and history to a host subject but never merges, splits or edits host records. Any merge decision informed by an active assertion is executed and owned by the host model.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Supplies Entity/Activity/Agent, wasAttributedTo, hadRole, wasRevisionOf, alternateOf, specializationOf, generatedAtTime and invalidatedAtTime as the alignment vocabulary for assertion transitions and authority attribution.

sources.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
sources.relevance: Defines generation, revision, attribution and invalidation ('the start of the destruction, cessation, or expiry of an existing entity'; the entity is no longer available for use after invalidation) and treats event times as optional instantaneous-event attributes - the basis for the retraction/tombstone divergence recorded as a conflict.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp format for every time-valued field: full date-time with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or 'Z'.

sources.title: RFC 8126 / BCP 26: Guidelines for Writing an IANA Considerations Section in RFCs
sources.relevance: Registry governance precedent: entries are marked deprecated or obsolete rather than removed, change control is named per entry, designated experts review requests against documented criteria, and reclamation or reuse of registered values is discouraged because deployed consumers depend on them.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 11179-6:2023 Information technology - Metadata registries (MDR) - Part 6: Registration
sources.relevance: Registration status is the state of an administered item in the view of the registration authority, split into lifecycle statuses (progression, e.g. Candidate, Recorded) and documentation statuses (no further progression, e.g. Retired, Superseded); establishes registration authority responsibility and mandatory-attribute entry conditions.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.relevance: Grounds graded equivalence: skos:exactMatch (high confidence of interchangeability across a wide range of applications, transitive, sub-property of closeMatch) versus skos:closeMatch (interchangeable in some applications), deliberately weaker than owl:sameAs - the predicate-strength axis the status qualifies.

sources.title: CCSDS 650.0-M-2, Reference Model for an Open Archival Information System (OAIS), Magenta Book
sources.organization: Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS); technically identical to ISO 14721
sources.relevance: Preservation Description Information (Reference, Provenance, Context, Fixity, Access Rights) grounds the requirement that history, integrity evidence and access conditions travel with the record and that provenance documents custody and change over time.

sources.title: Universal Electronic Records Management (ERM) Requirements
sources.organization: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)
sources.relevance: Lifecycle-structured records requirements (capture, maintenance and use, metadata, disposal, transfer) establishing that metadata must be captured and maintained across the lifecycle and that disposal follows an approved schedule rather than ad hoc deletion.

sources.title: Tombstone Pages (DataCite Support documentation)
sources.relevance: Normative practice that a registered persistent identifier cannot be deleted; after withdrawal the identifier must still resolve to a tombstone carrying the citation, the identifier in human- and machine-readable form and a stated reason for unavailability.

sources.title: Semantic Sensor Network Ontology (SOSA/SSN)
sources.relevance: sosa:phenomenonTime (when the result applies to the feature) versus sosa:resultTime (when the activity completed and the result became available) is the standards anchor for separating event/effective time from observation and ingestion time.

sources.title: DOI States (DataCite Support documentation)
sources.relevance: A worked identifier state machine (draft, registered, findable) in which only the pre-registration draft state is deletable and later states differ in resolvability and index visibility - precedent for pre-publication candidate discard versus post-publication irreversibility.

sources.title: The sameAs Problem: A Survey on Identity Management in the Web of Data
sources.organization: Beek, Raad, Wielemaker, van Harmelen et al. (arXiv preprint)
sources.relevance: Documents erroneous and contested owl:sameAs at web scale and the need for context-dependent, revisable identity links - the empirical case for a disputed status and for retaining refuting evidence.

bundles.name: Assertion status and controlled transitions
bundles.description: The status vocabulary that qualifies an alias/same-as assertion, the taxonomy of change kinds that move it, the matrix of allowed and forbidden transitions with entry and exit conditions, and the attribution of the authority recorded as responsible for each decision.
bundles.rationale: A registration authority's view of an administered item is expressed as a registration status split into progression and terminal categories, and registry practice marks entries deprecated or obsolete rather than removing them. An alias assertion is exactly such an administered item: consumers act on it, so its status and the conditions for changing it must be governed and explicit before any history can be meaningful.

layers.name: Status vocabulary and change-kind semantics
layers.description: Normative meaning of each status value, its consumption rule, and the disjoint kinds of change that can alter an assertion without deleting endpoints, rewriting history or erasing negative evidence.

findings.name: Canonical assertion status vocabulary
findings.description: Defines the governed status values for an alias/same-as assertion - candidate/proposed, under-review, active, disputed, superseded, retracted, rejected, expired, tombstoned - each with a normative definition, a category (progression versus terminal documentation status), and an explicit rule stating what a consuming agent may do with the equivalence while that status holds. Status qualifies the assertion record, never the identifiers it references.

questions.text: What is the normative meaning of each status value, and what may a consuming agent do with the asserted equivalence while that status holds?
answer_data: Status code from the governed code list
Consumption rule (may act, may act with caution, must not act, read-only historical)
Whether the status permits transitive chaining of the equivalence

questions.text: Is a given status a progression status that can still improve, or a terminal documentation status with no further progression?
answer_data: Permitted re-entry conditions if not strictly terminal

questions.text: Does the status apply to the whole assertion or only within a named scope, dataset or endpoint pair?
answer_data: Statement of whether an out-of-scope consumer may rely on the status

questions.text: Which external status or predicate vocabulary term does each local status map to, and where is that mapping only partial?
answer_data: Mapping relation (exact, close, broader, narrower, none)
Recorded divergence note where no faithful counterpart exists

data_elements.name: Assertion status code
data_elements.description: Governed code denoting the current lifecycle status of the assertion record.

data_elements.name: Status category
data_elements.description: Whether the status is a progression status or a terminal documentation status in the registration-authority sense.

data_elements.name: Consumption rule
data_elements.description: Normative instruction to consuming agents for this status, including whether the equivalence may be relied upon or chained.

data_elements.name: Status scope expression
data_elements.description: Named context, dataset or endpoint pair within which the status applies; absent means assertion-wide.

data_elements.name: Status term identifier
data_elements.description: Governed IRI of the status term in the owning registration authority's namespace; never reused or reassigned.

artifacts.name: Assertion status code list
artifacts.description: The published, versioned register of status terms with definitions, category, consumption rule and declared external mappings; the normative reference for producers and consumers of assertions.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each term carries a governed IRI in the registration authority's namespace; terms are never reused or reassigned after first publication, and superseded terms remain published with a deprecation marker. The register itself carries the authority's specification identifier plus a semantic version tag.

findings.name: Change-kind taxonomy and non-destruction rule
findings.description: Distinguishes the disjoint kinds of change that act on an assertion: correction (the record misstated the decision or facts), supersession (a newer assertion replaces this one), retraction (the assertion is withdrawn as wrong or unsupportable), endpoint-deprecation notice (a referenced endpoint was deprecated upstream), replacement/redirect notice (an endpoint was replaced upstream), authority withdrawal (the asserting party revokes its mandate or backing) and evidence expiry (the evidence validity horizon passed). No change kind may delete an endpoint reference, rewrite an earlier record or erase refuting evidence.

questions.text: How does this change differ from a correction, a supersession, a retraction, an endpoint-deprecation notice, a replacement/redirect notice, an authority withdrawal and an evidence expiry?
answer_data: Whether the earlier assertion is still considered to have been correct when made

questions.text: Which facets of the assertion does this change alter, and which facets must remain unchanged afterwards?
answer_data: Frozen facet list (identifier, endpoint references, prior decisions, prior reasons)

questions.text: What must never occur as a side effect of this change kind?
answer_data: Prohibited side effects (endpoint deletion, silent history rewrite, removal of refuting evidence, identifier reassignment)
Detection signal if a prohibited effect is attempted

questions.text: Which upstream model reported the event that triggered this change, and what reference points to that upstream record?

data_elements.name: Change kind code
data_elements.description: Governed code naming the kind of change applied to the assertion.

data_elements.name: Prior-validity claim
data_elements.description: Whether the change asserts the earlier state was wrong when made (correction, retraction) or correct when made but no longer current (supersession, expiry, deprecation).

data_elements.name: Upstream trigger reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the endpoint-registry, authority or evidence record whose event triggered the change; carried as a reference, never as a copy of that model's lifecycle.

data_elements.name: Frozen facet list
data_elements.description: Facets that the change kind must leave byte-identical, used as the validation contract for the change.

artifacts.name: Assertion change-kind code list
artifacts.description: Published register of change kinds with discriminating criteria, permitted target statuses, prior-validity semantics and the prohibited side effects for each kind.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI per change-kind term in the registration authority's namespace; deprecated kinds remain published and are never reassigned to a different meaning.

layers.name: Transition rules and decision-authority attribution
layers.description: The governed transition matrix with entry and exit conditions, the handling of forbidden transition attempts, and the recorded attribution of the authority responsible for each status decision.

findings.name: Allowed and forbidden transitions with entry and exit conditions
findings.description: The normative from-status/to-status matrix for the assertion lifecycle, with per-transition entry conditions (mandatory attributes, required evidence, required reviewer role), exit conditions (open obligations that block departure), terminality, and the rule that a forbidden attempt is recorded as a rejected transition rather than silently discarded. Post-publication statuses are not deletable; only a never-published candidate may be discarded, and then only if it was never externally referenced.

questions.text: Which target statuses are reachable from the current status, and which are explicitly forbidden?
answer_data: Forbidden to-status list with the reason each is forbidden

questions.text: What entry conditions must hold before a transition into this status can be recorded?
What open obligations block leaving this status?
answer_data: Open obligation list (unresolved dispute, missing successor link, pending evidence refresh)

questions.text: Is this status terminal, or may the assertion be re-opened, and on what recorded justification?
answer_data: Required justification text and authority level

questions.text: How is an attempted transition that the matrix forbids recorded and reported back to the requester?
answer_data: Whether the assertion status changed (it must not)

data_elements.name: From-status
data_elements.description: Status the assertion held immediately before the transition.

data_elements.name: To-status
data_elements.description: Status the assertion holds immediately after the transition.

data_elements.name: Transition permitted flag
data_elements.description: Whether the from/to pair is permitted by the governed matrix.

data_elements.name: Entry condition expression
data_elements.description: Machine-checkable condition that must hold before the transition is recordable.

data_elements.name: Exit obligation
data_elements.description: Outstanding obligation that must be discharged before the assertion may leave the status.

artifacts.name: Assertion state-transition matrix
artifacts.description: The versioned normative specification of permitted and forbidden transitions, entry and exit conditions, terminality and the rejected-transition recording rule.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the registration authority's specification identifier plus a semantic version tag; a revised matrix is a new version linked by supersedes/superseded-by and never an in-place edit, so historical records remain interpretable against the matrix version in force at decision time.

findings.name: Responsible authority attribution for a status decision
findings.description: Records which agent is held responsible for each status decision, in which role, under which mandate or delegation, and against which governing decision policy. Attribution is a provenance record: it names the responsible party and cites the policy, and it neither evaluates nor enforces whether that party was permitted to act, which the referenced access-policy model owns. Change control over the assertion record and over the status vocabulary is named separately per registry practice.

questions.text: Which agent is recorded as responsible for this status decision, and in what role?
answer_data: Agent reference into the agent registry
Role code held at decision time

questions.text: Which body holds change control over this assertion record and over the status vocabulary itself?
answer_data: Change controller reference for the assertion
Change controller reference for the vocabulary
Escalation path when the two differ

questions.text: Under which mandate, delegation or review policy was the deciding agent acting, and where is that policy referenced?
How is a multi-party or quorum review recorded when several reviewers contribute to one decision?

data_elements.name: Deciding agent reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent recorded as responsible for the transition; resolved in the external agent registry.

data_elements.name: Decision role code
data_elements.description: Role the agent held with respect to the decision, such as registrar, designated expert reviewer or records custodian.

data_elements.name: Mandate or delegation reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the mandate, delegation instrument or review policy under which the agent acted.

data_elements.name: Change controller reference
data_elements.description: Party holding change control over the assertion record, named per registry practice.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Authority attribution is a set of reference-valued fields carried inside the transition record; it produces no separate document. The agents, roles, mandates and decision policies it points to are maintained by the agent registry and the access-policy model, and reproducing them here would duplicate models that own their own lifecycle and evaluation semantics.

bundles.name: Immutable transition history and temporal reconstruction
bundles.description: The append-only history of status decisions, the evidence and link structures that must survive every change, the bitemporal frame separating effective validity from record time, and the handling of conflicts, late arrivals, rollback requests, authority loss and post-retraction readability.
bundles.rationale: Records requirements demand that lifecycle metadata be captured and maintained rather than overwritten, preservation description information requires provenance and fixity to travel with the record, and registered-identifier practice requires that a withdrawn item remain resolvable to a tombstone stating why. Together these make the transition history, not the current status field, the authoritative artefact of this model.

layers.name: Transition records, evidence and links
layers.description: Content, ordering and integrity of the append-only transition record, and the supersession, dispute and evidence references - including refuting evidence - that it must preserve.

findings.name: Immutable transition record content and integrity
findings.description: Each status decision produces exactly one append-only record carrying the assertion reference, monotonic ordinal, from-status, to-status, change kind, reason in the decider's own words, deciding agent and role, decision time, matrix version in force, and an integrity digest chained to its predecessor. Decided fields are never edited in place; a mistake is corrected by appending a correction record that references the target.

questions.text: What identifier and ordinal uniquely denote this transition record within the assertion's history?
answer_data: Monotonic ordinal within the assertion scope

questions.text: Which decision does the record describe, expressed as prior status, new status, change kind and outcome?
What reason and rationale were given at decision time, in the decider's own words?
answer_data: Language tag of the reason text

questions.text: By which recording procedure was the entry appended, checked and sealed?
answer_data: Matrix version in force at decision time

questions.text: How would tampering with an already-appended record be detected?

data_elements.name: Transition record identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier of one appended transition record.

data_elements.name: Transition ordinal
data_elements.description: Monotonically increasing sequence number of the record within the assertion's history; a sequence token, never a date.

data_elements.name: Decision reason
data_elements.description: Free-text reason recorded by the deciding agent at decision time and never rewritten afterwards.

data_elements.name: Record integrity digest
data_elements.description: Digest over the canonical serialisation of the record, chained to the predecessor digest to make silent alteration detectable.

data_elements.name: Matrix version in force
data_elements.description: Version tag of the transition matrix against which the decision was validated, so historical records stay interpretable.

artifacts.name: Assertion transition record entry
artifacts.description: One sealed, append-only entry in the assertion's history, carrying the decision, its attribution, its time coordinates and its integrity digest.
media_or_form: Serialised record in the adopting Dimension's store
artifacts.identity_strategy: Priority: the authoritative record identifier issued by the master system that owns the assertion register; otherwise a governed IRI in the owner namespace; otherwise a ULID minted by the adopting Dimension. Entries are ordered within an assertion by a zero-padded monotonic ordinal that carries no date component and is never reused, even after a rejected or rolled-back attempt.

findings.name: Evidence polarity and assertion-to-assertion links
findings.description: Every decision cites the evidence considered, separating supporting from refuting items with the strength assessed at decision time, and records the links between assertions: supersedes / superseded-by, disputes / disputed-by, corrects / corrected-by and replaced-by. Refuting evidence references are retained through retraction and tombstoning; a later positive decision never removes earlier negative evidence. Evidence content and its own lifecycle stay with the evidence and match models.

questions.text: Which evidence items were considered supporting and which refuting at the time of the decision?
What strength or confidence was assessed for each evidence item, and by which stated method?
Which assertion does this one supersede, and which assertion supersedes it?
answer_data: Whether the successor narrows, widens or reverses the equivalence

questions.text: For how long must refuting evidence references be preserved after the assertion is retracted or tombstoned?
answer_data: Policy owner reference for disposition execution

data_elements.name: Evidence reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an evidence item considered in the decision, held externally.

data_elements.name: Evidence polarity
data_elements.description: Whether the cited item supported or refuted the asserted equivalence.

data_elements.name: Supersedes / superseded-by reference
data_elements.description: Directed link between the assertion and the assertion that replaces or is replaced by it.

data_elements.name: Dispute reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the raised dispute, including the disputing party and the contested facet.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are reference-valued and link-valued fields inside transition records rather than a separate deliverable. The evidence documents, match scores and dispute cases they point to are produced and governed by the evidence, entity-resolution and case models; materialising local copies would duplicate content whose lifecycle and quality semantics belong to those models.

layers.name: Effective intervals and bitemporal record time
layers.description: Separation of the interval over which the equivalence is claimed to hold from the times at which decisions were made, observed and ingested, together with the reconstruction rules for late arrivals and retroactive corrections.

findings.name: Effective interval and bitemporal timestamps
findings.description: Each assertion carries an effective interval over which the equivalence is claimed to hold, and each transition record carries a decision/event time, an observation time and an ingestion time. All are RFC 3339 date-time values with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; the originating offset is preserved alongside any normalised UTC value. Open-ended intervals are represented explicitly as unbounded-at-this-time rather than as an unqualified null, and evidence-validity horizons drive expiry.

questions.text: Over which effective interval is the asserted equivalence claimed to hold?
answer_data: Basis for the interval (source validity, decision, evidence horizon)

questions.text: What are the decision time, the observation time and the ingestion time of this record, and where do they differ?
answer_data: Explanation of any material gap between them

questions.text: How must each time value be expressed, and what precision and offset must be present?
How is an unknown or open-ended interval endpoint represented without implying an unlimited claim?
answer_data: Reason for openness (not yet ended, unknown, pending review)

questions.text: When does the assertion expire automatically because its evidence-validity horizon has passed?
answer_data: Whether expiry is automatic or requires a recorded decision

data_elements.name: Effective-from
data_elements.description: Instant from which the asserted equivalence is claimed to hold, as an RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: Effective-to
data_elements.description: Instant at which the claim ceases to hold, or an explicit unbounded marker with a stated reason.

data_elements.name: Decision (event) time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the status decision was taken by the responsible authority.

data_elements.name: Observation time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the decision or upstream event became known to the recording system.

data_elements.name: Ingestion time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the record was committed to the store, establishing the as-known-at axis for reconstruction.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Temporal framing is expressed entirely as typed fields on assertions and transition records; it yields no separate document or media object. The clock authority, calendar services and any timestamping trust service are external and retain their own governance.

findings.name: Late arrivals, retroactive corrections and as-of reconstruction
findings.description: Handles events recorded after later events already exist and corrections that change what is believed to have been true in the past. Records are never reordered or overwritten: a late arrival is appended with its own decision time and a later ingestion time, and a retroactive correction appends a record that restates the effective interval or the corrected facts while pointing at the record it corrects. Two reconstructions are supported and must be distinguishable: the status as it was known at a past instant, and the status now believed to have applied at that instant.

questions.text: How is an event recorded after a later event already exists reconciled without reordering the history?
answer_data: Decision time versus ingestion time gap
Records whose interpretation changes as a result

questions.text: What procedure records a retroactive correction to a past effective interval or a past decision?
answer_data: Corrected field path and restated value
Statement that the original record remains readable

questions.text: How is the status as it was known at a past instant distinguished from the status now believed to have applied then?
answer_data: Set of records included in each reconstruction

questions.text: What signals a late arrival or correction to downstream consumers that already acted on the earlier state?

data_elements.name: Corrects reference
data_elements.description: Reference from a correction record to the earlier record whose content it restates; the earlier record remains readable.

data_elements.name: Late-arrival flag
data_elements.description: Marks a record whose decision time precedes the decision time of an already-committed later record.

data_elements.name: As-of event-time parameter
data_elements.description: Query coordinate selecting the effective state that applied at a given instant according to current belief.

data_elements.name: As-known-at parameter
data_elements.description: Query coordinate selecting the state as it was recorded and knowable at a given instant, excluding later arrivals.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Late arrival and retroactive correction are expressed through fields already present on appended records plus query coordinates over the two time axes; they create no additional artefact. Materialising a separate correction document would risk becoming a second, divergent source of truth alongside the append-only history.

layers.name: Conflicts, rollback, authority loss and tombstones
layers.description: Detection and representation of mutually inconsistent statuses, handling of rollback requests and authority loss, and the guaranteed readable remainder after retraction or tombstoning.

findings.name: Conflicting states, rollback requests, authority loss and post-retraction readability
findings.description: Covers two or more simultaneously recorded, mutually inconsistent statuses for the same assertion (typically from different authorities or a partitioned write path), which are represented as an explicit disputed state naming the conflicting records rather than being silently reconciled; rollback requests, which are satisfied by appending a forward transition that restores an earlier status with its own justification, never by removing records; authority loss or withdrawal, which freezes further transitions by that authority and marks affected assertions for review while leaving their history intact; and the tombstone, which keeps the assertion identifier resolvable and carries the identifier, terminal status, reason, effective interval, links and history pointer after retraction.

questions.text: How are two simultaneously recorded, mutually inconsistent statuses for one assertion detected and represented?
answer_data: Conflicting record references and their authorities
Representation rule (explicit disputed state, no silent reconciliation)

questions.text: What happens to an assertion when the authority that made it loses or withdraws its mandate?
answer_data: Freeze scope for further transitions by that authority
Statement that prior history remains unchanged and readable

questions.text: How is a rollback request satisfied when the append-only rule forbids removing records?
answer_data: Forward transition that restores the earlier status
List of records that remain in place

questions.text: Which fields remain readable, and to which audiences, after retraction or tombstoning?
answer_data: Always-readable field set (identifier, terminal status, reason, effective interval, links)
Audience classes and the policy reference governing them

questions.text: What minimum content must a tombstone retain, and under which retention class?
answer_data: Statement that the identifier is never reassigned

data_elements.name: Conflict identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a detected inconsistency between simultaneously recorded statuses for one assertion.

data_elements.name: Rollback request reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the request that prompted a restoring forward transition, retained with its outcome.

data_elements.name: Authority-withdrawal reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the record of an authority losing or withdrawing its mandate, with the affected scope.

data_elements.name: Tombstone reason
data_elements.description: Stated reason for unavailability shown on the tombstone, required so that a resolver confirms the identifier was found and explains its withdrawal.

data_elements.name: Post-tombstone readable field set
data_elements.description: Enumerated fields guaranteed to remain readable after retraction or tombstoning, subject to redaction of personal data.

artifacts.name: Assertion tombstone record
artifacts.description: The persistent notice that replaces an operational assertion after retraction: it keeps the identifier resolvable and presents the terminal status, the stated reason, the effective interval that once applied, supersession or replacement links and a pointer to the full history.
artifacts.identity_strategy: The tombstone carries the retracted assertion's own identifier unchanged so existing references keep resolving; the identifier is never deleted or reassigned. A distinct tombstone record identifier is minted for the notice itself, following the same identifier priority as other records of this model.

functions.name: Open assertion status
functions.description: Places a newly created alias/same-as assertion under lifecycle governance by recording its initial status and the first transition record.
preconditions: The assertion record exists and carries at least two endpoint references
Mandatory attributes required by the entry conditions for the initial status are present
A proposing agent with a recorded role is supplied
effects: The assertion becomes addressable with a governed status
History begins and is thereafter append-only
No endpoint, master-data or match record is created or altered

functions.name: Validate proposed transition
functions.description: Checks a proposed from/to transition against the governed matrix, its entry conditions and any open exit obligations, and returns a conformance verdict with reasons. The verdict is advisory to the recording process; it is not an authorization decision and it does not enforce anything.
outputs: Unmet entry conditions and outstanding exit obligations
preconditions: A published transition matrix version is resolvable
The current status is readable from the latest transition record
effects: Produces a verdict consumed by the append function
Non-conformant verdicts are retained for the rejected-transition record
Never changes the assertion status by itself

functions.name: Append transition record
functions.description: Seals and appends one immutable transition record for a validated status decision, including attribution, reason, both time axes and the chained integrity digest.
outputs: Sealed transition record with next ordinal
preconditions: The transition validated as conformant, or the record is explicitly typed as a rejected transition
All timestamps are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z
The predecessor record digest is retrievable
effects: History grows by exactly one entry; no earlier entry is modified
Current status is derived, not independently edited
Ordinals are never reused, including after rejection or rollback

functions.name: Resolve status as of a given time
functions.description: Reconstructs the assertion's status on either time axis: the status believed to have applied at a past instant, or the status as it was knowable at a past ingestion instant.
outputs: Resolved status for the requested axis
Flag when the two axes disagree
preconditions: At least one transition record exists
Both time coordinates are RFC 3339 values with seconds and explicit offset or Z
effects: Read-only reconstruction; no record is written
Late arrivals are included on the belief axis and excluded from the as-known-at axis

functions.name: Record supersession or replacement link
functions.description: Records the directed supersedes / superseded-by or replaced-by relationship between a retiring assertion and its successor, together with the status transition of the retiring assertion.
outputs: Transition record moving the predecessor to superseded
Statement of how the successor differs in scope or strength
preconditions: The successor assertion exists and is at least in a recordable status
The predecessor is not already in a terminal status that forbids supersession
effects: Both assertions remain readable and independently addressable
No endpoint is deleted and no redirect is executed

functions.name: Record retraction and raise tombstone
functions.description: Withdraws an assertion as wrong or unsupportable and raises the tombstone that keeps its identifier resolvable with a stated reason, terminal status, former effective interval, links and a history pointer.
outputs: Transition record moving the assertion to retracted
preconditions: The retraction is conformant with the transition matrix
A reason is supplied; an empty reason is not acceptable
Refuting evidence references, where they exist, are attached
effects: The identifier keeps resolving and is never reassigned
History, prior reasons and refuting evidence references remain readable
Disposition of the underlying storage remains with the retention policy owner

functions.name: Detect conflicting simultaneous statuses
functions.description: Identifies mutually inconsistent statuses recorded for the same assertion over overlapping effective intervals and represents the situation as an explicit dispute naming the conflicting records.
outputs: Conflict record with references to the conflicting decisions
preconditions: Two or more records assert statuses whose effective intervals overlap
Each conflicting record names its deciding authority
effects: The conflict is made visible rather than silently reconciled
No conflicting record is deleted, reordered or downgraded
Resolution requires a recorded decision by a competent authority

functions.name: Flag evidence expiry and review due
functions.description: Marks assertions whose evidence validity horizon or mandated review interval has passed, so that expiry is an explicit recorded state rather than a silent staleness.
preconditions: An evidence validity horizon or review interval is recorded
The evaluation instant is an RFC 3339 value with seconds and explicit offset or Z
effects: Expiry becomes a recorded transition with its own reason and time coordinates
The assertion remains readable with an altered consumption rule
Evidence content itself is neither re-evaluated nor modified here

composition.target: WM-XCT-011 (registered parent model of the alias/same-as family)
composition.purpose: Inherit the parent's subject framing and registry placement. The parent, not this model, defines the shared identifier-reference substrate; this model contributes the assertion-level status vocabulary, transition control and immutable history. The parent boundary is registry-declared and has no external primary description, so this link is recorded as a gap pending boundary review.

composition.target: Host entity, master-data or catalogue models carrying identifiers from multiple authorities
composition.purpose: Attach assertion status and transition history to host subjects without importing host identity semantics. The host owns creation, merge, split and any other mutation of its records; this mixin only records what was asserted, by whom, on what basis and in which status.

composition.target: Identifier and endpoint registration model (endpoint lifecycle, deprecation, redirect execution)
composition.purpose: Carry endpoint references and the binding between an assertion and its endpoints, plus the assertion-side consequence of an upstream deprecation or replacement notice. Endpoint status, permanence rules and any resolution or redirect execution remain owned by the endpoint registry.

Reference a match score or reconciliation result as evidence for a status decision, with the scoring method identifier. Similarity computation, thresholds, blocking and clustering remain owned by the resolution model.
Resolve the deciding agent, its role at decision time and its mandate or delegation instrument. Agent lifecycle, credentialing and organisational structure remain with the registry.

Cite the governing decision or access policy in the transition record so a reader can see under which rule the decision was framed. Evaluation of whether a principal may read or write, and any enforcement or access-audit record, remain wholly with that model.

composition.target: Retention, disposition and privacy model of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Carry the retention class and disposition authority references applicable to assertion records and tombstones. Scheduling, approval and physical execution of disposal or erasure are owned by that model; this model states only what must survive while a record is retained.

Declared, non-conformant alignment: transition records map to activities with qualified attribution, reasons and event times; supersession maps to revision. Invalidation is deliberately not used for retraction, because PROV invalidation means the entity is no longer available for use while a retracted assertion must stay readable as a tombstone.

Map local statuses onto registration-status categories - progression statuses versus terminal documentation statuses - and adopt the registration-authority view of who determines status. The mapping is partial: contested and withdrawn-authority states have no direct counterpart.

composition.target: SKOS mapping property vocabulary (exactMatch, closeMatch, related matches)
composition.purpose: Bind the asserted predicate strength to a standard mapping property so consumers can interpret how strong the claimed equivalence is. The status qualifies the assertion about the predicate; it does not redefine SKOS semantics or entail owl:sameAs.

composition.target: Preservation description information practice (OAIS Provenance and Fixity)
composition.purpose: Align the transition history and integrity digests with preservation description information so that provenance, fixity and access-rights context travel with an exported assertion. Archival ingest, storage and preservation planning remain with the archive.

owner_package_requirements: Name the registration authority that owns assertion status decisions, and name separately the change controller for the status vocabulary and the transition matrix.
Publish the status code list, the change-kind code list and the versioned transition matrix in the owner namespace before any assertion is recorded, and keep every superseded version resolvable.
Declare the retention class, disposition authority and tombstone policy for assertion records and transition history, including the minimum survival period for refuting evidence references.

Declare which external models own endpoint lifecycle, match computation, agent registry, authorization evaluation and disposition execution, so no local finding silently assumes those responsibilities.
Declare the clock source and offset policy used for decision, observation and ingestion timestamps.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Status terms, change kinds and matrix versions live under one stable namespace controlled by the adopting Dimension, for example {dimension-namespace}/alias-status/{term} and {dimension-namespace}/alias-transition-matrix/{version}. Terms are additive and permanent: a term is deprecated with a marker and a successor pointer, never removed, redefined or reassigned, because deployed consumers may already act on it. Assertion record identifiers live in a separate namespace from vocabulary terms so a record identifier can never be mistaken for a status term.
registry_links: Vercy registry entry vr.wm-xct-036 (model WM-XCT-036, entry kind mixin) and its recorded parent entry WM-XCT-011
Alignment registries: W3C PROV-O and PROV-DM, W3C SKOS, ISO/IEC 11179-6 registration statuses
Adopting-Dimension registries for agents and roles, endpoints, evidence items and retention classes

canonicalization_rules: Serialise a transition record for digest purposes in a deterministic canonical form: fixed field order, no insignificant whitespace, stable Unicode normalisation, and codes in lower-kebab-case.
Normalise every timestamp to UTC for comparison while retaining the originating RFC 3339 offset as recorded; comparison never rewrites the stored value.
Order history within an assertion by ordinal; where ordering by time is required, sort by decision time, then ingestion time, then ordinal, so late arrivals never displace an existing ordinal.
Resolve references by identifier, never by display label, so relabelling an agent, endpoint or evidence item cannot alter the meaning of a historical record.
patch_rules: The history is append-only: no in-place edit of status, change kind, reason, deciding agent, evidence references or time coordinates on a sealed record.
A mistake is corrected by appending a correction record that names the target record and the restated value; the original remains readable and retains its digest.

Only additive annotation fields (for example, cross-references added later, or redaction markers required by privacy law) may be attached to a sealed record, and each annotation is itself an appended, attributed entry.
Redaction required by law replaces a value with an explicit redaction marker that preserves record structure, field presence and the digest history; it never removes the record or its links.
A rollback is expressed as a forward transition restoring an earlier status with its own reason and attribution; removing or reordering records is not a permitted patch.
compatibility_rules: Adding a status term, change kind or optional field is a minor change; removing or redefining a term is breaking and must instead be handled by deprecation with a successor pointer.
Loosening the transition matrix is minor; tightening it is breaking, and historical records remain interpreted against the matrix version recorded as in force at decision time.
Consumers must treat an unrecognised status as non-actionable rather than defaulting to active, and must not chain an equivalence whose status is unknown to them.
Exports must carry the status term namespace and matrix version alongside the records, so a receiving system can interpret the history without access to live vocabulary services.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the identifier issued by the master system of record that owns the assertion register, used whenever such a system exists.
Governed global identifier or IRI: a resolvable IRI in the owner namespace, or a governed persistent identifier such as a DOI or Handle where the assertion is published externally.

UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension when neither an authoritative master-system identifier nor a governed global identifier is available; the minted value is then registered and never reassigned.
A date, a version label, a status term or a natural-key string is never an identifier; identifiers are opaque and stable across every status change including retraction and tombstoning.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Every time-valued field is an RFC 3339 date-time including seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; local times without an offset are rejected. Event time (the decision or upstream event instant) is recorded separately from observation time (when it became known to the recording system) and ingestion time (when the record was committed), and all three are retained when they differ, so a late-arriving decision keeps its true event time while remaining ordered correctly on the as-known-at axis. The originating offset is preserved alongside any normalised UTC value.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Transition records are serialised by a monotonically increasing, zero-padded ordinal scoped to the assertion (for example ordinal 000017 of assertion X). Ordinals are allocated at append time, are never reused - including after a rejected or rolled-back transition - and carry no date, year, quarter or other temporal component. Tombstones are not serialised: an assertion has at most one tombstone, identified by the assertion identifier plus a distinct tombstone record identifier.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each sealed record carries a digest over its canonical form together with its predecessor's digest, forming a verifiable chain per assertion. Verification failure never triggers deletion or repair in place: the record is flagged integrity-suspect, the discrepancy is recorded as an appended entry with its detection time, and remediation follows the adopting Dimension's records procedure. Fixity checks are executed by the platform storage service; this model defines only what must be verifiable.

policies: History immutability: once appended, a transition record is never edited, reordered or removed; every later change is an additional attributed record.

Non-erasure of negative evidence: refuting evidence references and rejected or disputed decisions survive supersession, retraction and tombstoning, so a subsequent positive decision can never conceal earlier contradiction.
Tombstone rather than delete: a published assertion identifier keeps resolving after withdrawal and presents the terminal status and a stated reason; identifiers are never reassigned.
No silent endpoint effects: no status change deletes, deprecates or redirects an endpoint; upstream endpoint events are recorded as references and consequences only.

Authority loss freezes rather than rewrites: when an authority's mandate is withdrawn, further transitions by that authority are barred and affected assertions are marked for review, while all prior records remain intact and readable.
Explicit conflict: mutually inconsistent statuses are represented as a disputed state naming the conflicting records rather than resolved silently by recency or precedence.

read: Default read returns the current derived status, its consumption rule, the effective interval and a pointer to the full history.
As-of reads are supported on both time axes and must state which axis was used: the status believed to have applied at an event instant, or the status as knowable at an ingestion instant.

Retracted and tombstoned assertions remain readable, presenting the terminal status, the stated reason, former effective interval and links; readers must be able to distinguish a tombstone from an unknown identifier.
Whether a given principal may perform any of these reads is decided by the referenced access-policy model, not here.
create: Creation records the initial status with a first transition record; a status may not exist without a record explaining how it arose.
Mandatory at creation: assertion reference, at least two endpoint references, predicate strength, proposing agent and role, reason, effective interval basis and RFC 3339 time coordinates.
A never-published candidate that has never been externally referenced may be discarded before first publication; once published or externally referenced, the identifier becomes permanent.
update: There is no in-place update of a decided field; every change is an appended transition, correction or annotation record with its own attribution, reason and time coordinates.
The current-status field is a derived projection of the history and must never be written independently of an appended record.
An attempted transition forbidden by the matrix is recorded as a rejected transition with the violated rule and the requester, and leaves the status unchanged.
delete: This model defines no destructive delete for sealed transition records, tombstones or published assertion identifiers; withdrawal is expressed as retraction plus tombstone, and the identifier remains resolvable and unreassigned.

The only deletable object is an unpublished candidate assertion that was never externally referenced and has no sealed decision beyond its own creation record; the discard is itself recorded as an appended entry.

Retention, disposition scheduling and the physical execution of destruction or transfer are owned by the adopting Dimension's retention and disposition model and its records authority, following an approved schedule rather than ad hoc deletion; this model contributes only the retention class reference and the minimum content a tombstone must keep.

Statutory erasure of personal data (for example a reviewer's identity or a reason text naming a person) executes under the adopting Dimension's privacy model and is applied as redaction markers that preserve record structure, ordinals, links and digest history; it never removes a transition record or a tombstone.
Platform access logs about who read or wrote these records have their own retention rule owned by the platform audit service and are outside this model's boundary.

roles.name: Registration authority / status steward
responsibilities: Determine and record the registration status of assertions in accordance with the published matrix
Own the status and change-kind vocabularies and their versioned publication
Approve re-opening of a non-terminal status and resolve disputed states by recorded decision

roles.name: Designated reviewer
responsibilities: Assess supporting and refuting evidence against documented criteria before a transition to active
Record a reasoned decision, including dissent in quorum reviews
Raise a dispute when evidence contradicts an active assertion

roles.name: Records custodian
responsibilities: Ensure history is appended, sealed and verifiable, and that no record is edited in place
Apply retention classes, tombstones and lawful redaction markers as instructed by the retention and privacy owners
Escalate integrity-suspect records and preserve evidence of the discrepancy

roles.name: Assertion producer / proposing agent
responsibilities: Create assertions with complete mandatory attributes, predicate strength and evidence references
Report upstream endpoint deprecation, replacement and authority-withdrawal events as references
Request corrections and rollbacks through recorded requests rather than direct edits

roles.name: Consuming integrator
responsibilities: Honour the per-status consumption rule and treat unknown statuses as non-actionable
Subscribe to change notifications and re-evaluate decisions after late arrivals, corrections and retractions
Resolve tombstones correctly and never treat a tombstoned identifier as unknown

access.default_rule: Transition history and status are readable by any principal already permitted to read the assertion record, and are at least as open as the assertion itself; write access is limited to the authority recorded as competent for the transition. The permission decision itself is evaluated and enforced by the referenced access-policy model, which this model only cites.
exceptions: Deliberation material attached to an under-review status may be restricted until the decision is recorded, while the resulting decision, reason and attribution become readable with the record.
Reason texts or reviewer identities containing personal data may be redacted with explicit markers for wider audiences, preserving record structure, ordinals and digests.
Dispute evidence under legal or commercial embargo may be reference-only for general readers, with the existence of the dispute always visible.
A tombstone for an assertion that was publicly readable remains publicly readable; withdrawal must not be used to make a formerly public identifier silently unresolvable.
audit_requirements: Reads and writes of these records are logged by the adopting Dimension's platform audit service under its own retention rule; this model neither defines nor owns audit-trail semantics.

The domain transition history is not a substitute for the platform access audit trail, and the audit trail is not a substitute for the transition history; both must exist and neither may be reconstructed from the other.
Any lawful redaction or integrity-suspect flag applied to a record is itself recorded as an appended, attributed entry so the intervention remains visible.

required_fields: Status vocabulary and transition matrix URL
read_order: AGENTS.md - identify the model, its owner and where each contract lives
Specification URL - model boundary, status vocabulary, change kinds and transition matrix with the version in force
Storage type URL - how records, ordinals, digests and time fields are projected into the chosen store, which is a projection and not the semantics
Interface URL - how to read status, reconstruct as-of state on both time axes and submit transition proposals
Processes URL - recording, correction, supersession, retraction, tombstone, conflict resolution and rollback procedures with their responsible roles

coverage.claim: This structure covers the assertion lifecycle and immutable transition history of the WM-XCT-036 alias/same-as mixin as far as public primary standards support: status vocabulary and consumption rules, change-kind taxonomy, permitted and forbidden transitions with entry and exit conditions, responsible-authority attribution, append-only transition records with integrity chaining, evidence polarity and supersession links, bitemporal time handling, late arrivals and retroactive corrections, and conflict, rollback, authority-loss and tombstone handling. It is grounded in registration-status practice, registry permanence practice, provenance and preservation description information, records-management lifecycle requirements and internet timestamp format rules. It is not a claim of completeness: several nodes are supported by analogy from adjacent registry domains rather than by a standard written for identity assertions.

checklist.notes: Identifier priority runs authoritative master-system identifier, then governed IRI or persistent identifier, then minted UUID/ULID; ordinals are sequence tokens, never dates; identifiers survive retraction and are never reassigned.
All nine required statuses are defined with categories, consumption rules, entry and exit conditions, terminality and a governed transition matrix, plus explicit handling of forbidden attempts.
Supersedes/superseded-by, corrects/corrected-by, disputes/disputed-by and replaced-by links are modelled; endpoint, agent, evidence and policy relations are references to models that own them.
Effective interval separated from decision, observation and ingestion time; RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z; open intervals explicit; as-of reconstruction on both axes.
Every transition carries deciding agent, role, mandate reference, reason in the decider's own words and the matrix version in force, aligned to PROV attribution without claiming conformance.
Registration authority, change controller for records and for the vocabulary, and the external owners of endpoints, matching, authorization and disposition are named separately.
Entry-condition checks, matrix conformance verdicts, rejected-transition records and digest-chain verification with an integrity-suspect flag rather than repair in place.
Default read parity with the assertion, write limited to the recorded competent authority, four exception classes; the permission decision is evaluated by the referenced access-policy model.

No destructive delete of sealed records or published identifiers; tombstone minimum content defined; only never-published, never-referenced candidates are discardable; scheduling, disposal and statutory erasure execute under the adopting Dimension's retention and privacy models.

Declared partial alignments to PROV, SKOS mapping properties and ISO/IEC 11179-6 registration statuses; exports carry the vocabulary namespace and matrix version; unknown statuses must be treated as non-actionable.
Append-only patch rules, canonical serialisation, chained digests, non-reused ordinals and appended annotation for every later intervention including redaction.
Evidence polarity is explicit and refuting references are preserved through supersession, retraction and tombstoning.
Conflicting simultaneous statuses, invalid transitions, late arrivals, retroactive corrections, rollback requests and authority loss all resolve to appended records, never to silent reconciliation.
Mandate, delegation and quorum are recorded as attribution; the model deliberately does not evaluate whether the agent was permitted to act.

Evidence strength and predicate confidence are carried as referenced values with a stated method, but no primary standard fixes a confidence scale for identity assertions; the scale remains an adopting-Dimension choice.

Personal data may appear in reviewer identities and reason texts, but privacy classification, lawful basis and erasure decisions belong to the adopting Dimension's privacy model; only the redaction-marker mechanism is specified here.

known_omissions: The boundary of the registered parent model WM-XCT-011 could not be verified from any public source, so the CHILD link is declared as a gap pending boundary review; some identity-substrate concepts may belong there rather than here.

No consulted primary standard defines a disputed status for identity assertions. The disputed state is supported by analogy from registration-status practice and by empirical evidence of contested sameAs links, and is marked as a structural gap rather than canonical.
Quorum sizes, reviewer independence rules and escalation thresholds are left to the adopting Dimension; the consulted sources describe designated-expert review but do not fix quorum mechanics.
Cryptographic notarisation, external timestamping authorities and countersignature of transition records are deliberately excluded; only a digest chain is required.
No confidence or strength scale is prescribed for evidence or predicate strength, so cross-Dimension comparability of confidence values is not guaranteed.
Machine-readable serialisations of the status vocabulary and transition matrix are required to exist but their concrete syntax is a projection decision, not fixed here.
Bulk or federated propagation of a retraction to downstream caches is described only as a notification obligation; no delivery guarantee is defined.
conflicts: PROV-DM states that after invalidation an entity is no longer available for use, whereas this model requires a retracted assertion to remain readable as a tombstone. Retraction is therefore aligned to a terminal status plus tombstone rather than to prov invalidation; the divergence is declared, not resolved.

ISO/IEC 11179-6 registration statuses cover progression and terminal documentation states such as Candidate, Recorded, Retired and Superseded but provide no counterpart for disputed, retracted or authority-withdrawn assertions, so the alignment is explicitly partial.

SKOS deliberately avoids owl:sameAs because it is too strict, while many federated deployments publish owl:sameAs for the same intent. A status vocabulary cannot repair that semantic difference, so predicate strength must be recorded independently of status.

Registry practice discourages reclaiming registered values, while DataCite permits deleting a draft DOI before registration. This model resolves the tension narrowly: only a never-published, never-referenced candidate may be discarded, and the discard is itself recorded.

Records-management disposal duties can require eventual destruction of records that this model would otherwise keep readable indefinitely; the retention and disposition owner prevails, and the tombstone minimum is asserted only for the retention period in force.

Statutory erasure rights can conflict with the non-erasure of reviewer identities and reason texts; the model resolves this by redaction markers that preserve structure, which some regulators may still consider insufficient.
regional_assumptions: The NARA universal electronic records management requirements are United States federal guidance; other jurisdictions impose different schedules, approval authorities and transfer duties, and the retention statements here must be re-derived locally.

European data-protection erasure and objection rights are assumed to be capable of forcing redaction of person-identifying fields inside otherwise immutable records; the redaction-marker mechanism is the assumed accommodation and has not been tested against a specific supervisory decision.

Persistent-identifier practice is drawn from the scholarly DOI ecosystem; sectors using other identifier schemes may permit deletion or reassignment, which would break the tombstone guarantee and must be declared by the adopting Dimension.

Offsets are assumed to be recordable at source; where a legacy system supplies local time without an offset, the adopting Dimension must supply and record the offset determination rule rather than assuming UTC.
adversarial_checks: Checked every finding and function against the composition ledger for target-owned concepts: none defines endpoint lifecycle, deprecation of an endpoint itself, redirect execution, similarity or match computation, authorization evaluation, enforcement or master-data mutation. Endpoint deprecation and replacement appear only as referenced upstream triggers with assertion-side consequences.

Checked that citing an access policy or an audit service grants no ownership: the authority finding records attribution and cites policy only, the validate-transition function returns an advisory conformance verdict rather than a permission decision, and the access layer states explicitly that the platform audit service owns audit-trail semantics.

Attempted to break the append-only claim with rollback, correction and lawful erasure. Rollback is a forward restoring transition, correction is an appended restatement, erasure is a redaction marker preserving structure and digests; none removes or reorders a record, so the claim survives.

Tested whether a retraction could be used to hide an inconvenient assertion: the tombstone must remain resolvable with a stated reason, refuting evidence references survive, and a formerly public identifier may not become silently unresolvable.

Tested whether any identifier or serial token is date-derived: ordinals are monotonic integers scoped to an assertion with an explicit prohibition on temporal components, and the identifier priority states that a date, version label or status term is never an identifier.

Tested conformance overreach: PROV, SKOS, ISO/IEC 11179-6 and OAIS appear only as ALIGN links with named partiality, and the recorded conflicts show where alignment fails rather than asserting compliance.

Tested for duplication of the parent model: because the WM-XCT-011 boundary is unverifiable from public sources, identity-substrate concepts were deliberately left out and the link is declared a gap rather than modelled locally.
